messages:
sarah: Heads up — we have a ~118,742 USD timing gap on ResellerCo marketplace fees for Feb. GCP statement shows the fee applied 02/28 but our AR shows it as a March credit. Can someone look into invoice alignment?
liam: I can take a first pass. Do you have the invoice IDs?
alex: I pulled the raw statement earlier, looks like two lines that offset across month boundaries. Sending a quick snippet.
alex: ```
InvoiceID,Partner,Product,Amount,InvoiceDate
INV-2026-02-17,ResellerCo,GCP-Commitments,-118742.00,2026-02-28
INV-2026-03-05,MarketplaceAdjust,ResellerCo,118742.00,2026-03-05
```
maria: @liam FYI partner contract says marketplace settlements run in partner timezone (PST) and our GL uses UTC posting. Might explain the 1–5 day drift on cutoffs.
liam: Good point. I'll run a quick query to confirm posting vs statement dates.
liam: ```sql
SELECT invoice_id, SUM(amount) as total, invoice_date, posting_date
FROM `company_billing.marketplace_lines`
WHERE partner = 'ResellerCo' AND invoice_date BETWEEN '2026-02-01' AND '2026-03-10'
GROUP BY invoice_id, invoice_date, posting_date;
```
sarah: Thanks. This matters because it impacts reserved capacity commit reconciliation — ops budget reported Feb vs Mar changes the headroom.
alex: Confirmed: marketplace portal shows the charge on 02/28, but partner settlement (their payout report) posted as 03/05. There's an intermediary adjustment record on 03/05 that offsets the Feb invoice.
partners-support: (automated) Opened ticket with GCP Marketplace partner support: TICKET-8472. They confirmed settlements can post on partner payout schedule up to 7 days later.
maria: Action items: 1) liam to run full join of statement vs our GL by EOD, 2) alex to prepare reversal journal suggestion for Feb vs Mar split, 3) sarah to notify accounting about expected variance in Feb close.
liam: Running the join now — will post results here. Initial estimate: variance driven by timezone + partner payout cadence, not a true lost revenue event. :white_check_mark:
